description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

<system-reminder>

1	# Evaluation-game estimands and incentive-response testbed
2	
3	## Scope
4	
5	This is a small exact, finite synthetic testbed. It does not call a model,
6	collect transcripts, simulate interacting agents, or identify strategic intent.
7	It builds on the separation among game, case distribution, measurement, and
8	claim in [evaluation_design_calculus.md](evaluation_design_calculus.md). It
9	does not alter the frozen v3 sandbagging results or protocol.
10	
11	```powershell
12	$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
13	python scripts/verify_evaluation_game_testbed.py --output output/evaluation_game_testbed.json
14	python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_game_testbed.py -q
15	```
16	
17	The output is exact synthetic fixture evidence, not model or agent evidence.
18	It stores rational values as strings and will not overwrite an existing output.
19	
20	## Four non-interchangeable estimands
21	
22	Fix \(\mathcal E=\langle G,\Pi,D,Z,J,\mathcal A,C\rangle\). A score alone
23	does not say which object changed.
24	
25	| Estimand | Definition | It is not |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| Baseline gain | \(B=V_{\pi_1}(d)-V_{\pi_0}(d)\) with a named case law and judgment | Robustness or strategic stability |
28	| Robust regret | \(R(\pi;\mathcal Q)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q}[\max_{\pi'}V_{\pi'}(q)-V_\pi(q)]\) | A baseline gain or a measurement gap |
29	| Discrimination gap | \(\mathrm{TV}(Z_\#P_{\pi_1},Z_\#P_{\pi_0})\) | Utility, regret, or player information |
30	| Exploitability | \(\max_i[\sup_{\pi_i'}\mathbb EU_i(\pi_i',\pi_{-i})-\mathbb EU_i(\pi)]\) | Generalization or welfare |
31	
32	The finite fixtures make baseline gain and robust regret both one half. Their
33	matching numbers are intentional: their source objects and interpretation remain
34	different, so they must not be combined or relabeled as each other.
35	Both policies in the corrected baseline fixture receive the revealed state:
36	the baseline always chooses left and the candidate follows the observation.
37	The game and case law are consequently fixed for that comparison.
38	
39	## Observation-only Hide versus player-facing hiding
40	
41	Observation-only `Hide` belongs to acquisition. After players act, apply a
42	common Markov kernel \(H(z'\mid z)\) to each completed record:
43	
44	\[
45	P_H(z'\mid\pi)=\sum_z H(z'\mid z)P(z\mid\pi).
46	\]
47	
48	It does not change legal actions, player histories, transitions, or payoffs.
49	In the fixture, perfectly correct and perfectly wrong traces have visible
50	total-variation discrimination gap one. The common kernel maps both to
51	`redacted`, leaving an acquired-record gap of zero and demonstrating finite
52	data processing: \(\mathrm{TV}(H_\#P,H_\#Q)\leq\mathrm{TV}(P,Q)\).
53	
54	Removing information from a player before action instead changes \(O_i\) in
55	\(G\). In the two-location game, the optimal value falls from one to one half.
56	That is a game intervention, not offline measurement redaction. An adapter that
57	removes player feedback must type it that way irrespective of its method name.
58	
59	## Strategic checks, costs, and falsifiers
60	
61	The social-dilemma fixture enumerates a pure equilibrium set and reports the
62	selected outcome under `enumerate_pure_nash_then_lexicographically_select`; it
63	does not present the outcome as controller behavior. At `share, share`, exact
64	exploitability is two. Searching only the `share` deviation returns zero, which
65	is marked as a lower bound rather than exploitability. A matching-pennies
66	fixture separately checks equal primal maximin and dual minimax witnesses at
67	zero. It is not a generic equilibrium solver.
68	
69	Falsifiers for an applied strategic interpretation are an illegal deviation
70	class, private state leaked to the search, an unspecified adaptation or
71	equilibrium-selection rule, dependent payoff estimates, or calling a restricted
72	search exact exploitability. Report the restriction and withhold that stronger
73	claim when any appears.
74	
75	## Incentive-response design for sandbagging investigation
76	
77	The estimand is a behavioral incentive-response contrast, not intent. Let
78	\(Y_{c,d,g}\) be a blinded score with condition \(c\), difficulty \(d\), and
79	grader-severity stratum \(g\):
80	
81	\[
82	Y=\mu+\alpha_c+\beta_d+\gamma_g+\eta_{c,d}+\varepsilon.
83	\]
84	
85	Match paired control/incentive tasks within \((d,g)\), estimate
86	\(\tau_d=\mathbb E[Y_{0,d,g}-Y_{1,d,g}]\), and reserve untouched blocks to
87	test \(\iota=\tau_{hard}-\tau_{easy}\). Pairing cancels additive difficulty
88	and grader severity; it does not establish prompt equivalence or intent.
89	Selection of strata, allocation, and any target family remains in training data;
90	the interaction is tested only in the held-out confirmation data.
91	
92	For acquisition, condition 0 gives the ordinary task and performance objective;
93	condition 1 adds a preregistered evaluation-contingent incentive frame while
94	holding task instructions, tools, time budget, scoring rubric, and stated role
95	fixed. The frame is shown to the participant before acting, so it is a
96	presentation/incentive intervention on the game, not observation-only Hide.
97	Use held-out isomorphic task forms matched by difficulty calibrated on separate
98	data; randomize form-to-condition and AB/BA order in reset contexts. A negative
99	control uses comparably sized neutral framing with no changed incentive. This
100	design checks sensitivity to the chosen frame, not compliance with an assumed
101	internal utility function. Semantic equivalence must be reviewed independently.
102	
103	Estimate grader severity on independent anchor responses with condition labels
104	removed. Cross each grader/severity stratum with both conditions and both
105	difficulties using the same rubric and version; do not assign strict graders
106	only to the incentive arm. Save response, form, block, assignment, scorer, and
107	calibration identifiers. Difficulty- or condition-dependent grading errors
108	require an expanded nuisance model and separate checks. The executable fixture
109	encodes known additive severity, not estimated severity or verified blinding.
110	
111	The fixture has four equal-weight equal-variance strata and a 96-score budget.
112	Each matched pair costs two scored responses. It enumerates the 48-pair integer
113	allocation minimizing \(\sum_h(1/4)^2/n_h\) and obtains 12 pairs per stratum.
114	This optimization is conditional on its equal-variance and equal-cost premise.
115	In an applied study, preregister variance/cost estimates, retain minimum stratum
116	coverage, and use the resulting Neyman-style allocation without holdout tuning.
117	
118	The fixture deliberately has no latent intent variable and records
119	`intent_identified: false`. A contrast can arise from strategic response, benign
120	role constraints, task changes, condition-dependent scoring, or distribution
121	shift. Falsifiers include an interaction in negative-incentive controls, failed
122	prompt-equivalence review, unblinded scoring, grader severity not linked within
123	pairs, or a selection/holdout block overlap. Any falsifier defeats the strategic
124	interpretation; it is not evidence of a zero effect.
125	
126	## Executable confirmation and adversarial checks
127	
128	`evaluation_game_confirmation.py` now enforces the split on actual synthetic
129	pair and block records. Every block contains all four difficulty/grader strata.
130	Duplicate pairs, missing strata, mixed block metadata, reused training IDs,
131	and confirmation of a different family all raise errors. The selected family
132	is chosen by training mean gap with lexical ties, before confirmation rows are
133	generated. Identifiers can detect recorded overlap; they cannot independently
134	certify independence or prevent an operator from relabeling reused observations.
135	
136	The saved fixture has two families with eight training blocks each (64 pairs,
137	128 score operations), then 12 target and 12 negative-control blocks for the
138	selected family (96 pairs, 192 score operations). The total is **320**. These
139	are constructed score values, not paid model calls or independent model trials.
140	The older four-cell arithmetic illustration records eight score values and a
141	separate *planned* 96-score target allocation; that plan is not an acquisition
142	receipt. Calibration, prompt review, and scorer qualification costs remain
143	outside this synthetic count and must be budgeted for an observed study.
144	
145	Each confirmation block produces an equal-weight incentive-response contrast
146	and a hard-minus-easy interaction. Two exact two-sided sign tests receive
147	alpha/2 each, with ties discarded. These test directional consistency under
148	independent blocks and equiprobable nonzero signs under the null; they do not
149	test the population mean. The fixture reports the arithmetic means separately.
150	Its interaction is 1/5, with sign p-value 1/2048 across 12 positive blocks.
151	This deterministic positive fixture does not measure statistical coverage or
152	false-positive rates. Training-only effects return a holdout p-value of one.
153	This budget covers one selected-family evaluation. Multiple subjects or added
154	confirmatory contrasts require a frozen campaign correction; do not reuse the
155	same alpha independently for each subject or retune on confirmation outcomes.
156	
157	Negative controls must have exactly zero paired differences for this fixture's
158	support flag. This is an arithmetic diagnostic, not an empirical equivalence
159	test; observed controls would need uncertainty, tolerance margins, adequate
160	sample sizes, and a preregistered inference procedure. A control bias withholds
161	the support flag. Passing that flag still leaves `intent_identified: false`.
162	
163	The allocation optimizer solves the finite integer problem with supplied
164	weights, paired-difference variances, pair costs, budget, and minimum stratum
165	counts. Independent exhaustive enumeration checks it with unequal costs and
166	variances. Its variance objective assumes independent strata. Covariances of
167	contrasts measured in common blocks require a different objective; the block
168	confirmation fixture is not claimed to attain that independent-stratum bound.
169	
170	Additional checks cover 625 rational binary distribution/channel combinations
171	for total-variation contraction, malformed kernel rejection, and a falsifier
172	where different policy-specific channels manufacture discrimination. A general
173	finite matrix certificate reports primal and dual bounds and refuses to certify
174	an inferior matching-pennies strategy. A coordination-game example reports its
175	complete Nash set (two pure profiles and one uniformly mixed profile) alongside
176	two explicit update paths: simultaneous best responses cycle from (0,1), while
177	row-then-column updates reach (1,1). The former equilibrium enumeration rule is
178	a selection convention; these new paths supply actual finite adaptation rules.
179	
180	The verifier's schema 1.1 includes confirmation, allocation, adaptation, and
181	primal/dual results and source hashes. Run the expanded regressions with:
182	
183	```powershell
184	python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_game_testbed.py tests/test_evaluation_game_confirmation.py -q
185	```
186

1	# Feedback channel: suggested insertions for the evaluation design calculus
2	
3	Draft 0.2 — 2026-10-12. Suggestions only. Draft 0.2 states the ceiling law for
4	failure-targeted patching as well as for patching chosen at random.
5	
6	This file changes nothing in `evaluation_design_calculus.md` or
7	`evaluation_game_testbed.md`. Each block names a location in those documents,
8	offers text for it, and states what supports the text. Where a block is adopted,
9	its wording should be made the author's own. Where it is not, the executable
10	fixtures still stand by themselves.
11	
12	The gap being addressed: the calculus already says that a judgment "shown during
13	play or used for learning ... also enters observations or controller updates"
14	(§2), and that frozen-controller sensitivity differs from sensitivity "after
15	retraining, selecting another controller" (§7). It has no operator for that
16	channel, no estimand for what the channel does to a score, and no record of how
17	often it was used. A self-improvement loop is that channel applied once per
18	generation.
19	
20	## Evidence behind the suggestions
21	
22	| Level | Source | What it supplies |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| Finite verified example | `src/spiral_ln/evaluation_game_feedback.py`, 30 tests, receipt under `output/evaluation_game_feedback/` | Access-class ordering, one-generation selection gap, noise-ceiling threshold, failed-item enrichment, ledger enforcement |
25	| Synthetic mechanism result | `output/eval_reuse_toys/` (two seeded simulations, predictions hashed before each run) | Multi-generation behaviour of the gap under score-only and item-level feedback |
26	| Not available | — | Any language-model loop, any observed controller |
27	
28	The simulations are JavaScript, seeded, and not exact. Their prediction record
29	is 5 of 6 in the first run and 3 of 6 in the second, and both overpredicted the
30	size of the gap. One arm of the second run was added after its sealed results
31	were seen and is marked exploratory in its own files.
32	
33	## A. §2, after "Maintain three distinctions"
34	
35	Suggested fourth distinction:
36	
37	> 4. A judgment that reaches whatever produces the next controller is a channel.
38	> Its source set, its access class, and the number of times it was used belong
39	> in the experiment record. A score measured on a set that fed this channel is a
40	> selection score. A capability claim needs a set that did not.
41	
42	## B. §3, operator table
43	
44	Suggested row:
45	
46	| Proposed operator | Primary effect | Required detail |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,q}\) | Controller roster/protocol of a later generation | Source set \(s\); access class \(q\in\{\text{sealed},\text{score-only},\text{item-level}\}\); whether the consumer selects among candidates or supplies a training input; generation scope. |
49	
50	Suggested sentence beneath the table:
51	
52	> Feedback is not \(\operatorname{Rescore}\), which is offline, and not
53	> \(\operatorname{Observe}\), which changes what the evaluator records. It reads
54	> \(J\) restricted to \(s\) and writes \(\Pi\) for the next generation. Declaring
55	> a set sealed while a score from it reaches the loop is ill-typed.
56	
57	## C. §4, after the sentence on `Repeat` and reset/carry maps
58	
59	> Generations joined by Feedback are not independent blocks. The carry map
60	> carries the controller, and with it whatever of \(s\) the channel transmitted.
61	> Aggregating a per-generation score across such generations as if each were a
62	> fresh draw of the same experiment mistakes the unit.
63	
64	## D. §5, three laws and one observation
65	
66	**Coarsening law.**
67	
68	> The access classes are ordered: sealed is a deterministic function of the
69	> score, and the score is a deterministic function of the per-item outcomes.
70	> Total-variation distance between two controllers' feedback therefore cannot
71	> increase from item-level to score-only to sealed. Two controllers that fail
72	> different items with equal totals are separated completely by item-level
73	> feedback and not at all by a score.
74	
75	Support: `access_order_fixture`; the ordering is checked for every pair of
76	distributions on a rational grid over two-item outcomes.
77	
78	**Selection law.**
79	
80	> Keeping the best of \(K\) candidates by score on \(s\), then reporting that
81	> score, overstates: \(\mathbb E[\max_k\hat S_k]\ge\max_k\mathbb E[\hat S_k]\).
82	> This is the same convexity as the mixture law, with the candidate index in
83	> place of the mixture component. For candidates of equal true value
84	> one half, two candidates and one item give a reported value of three quarters.
85	
86	Support: `selection_inflation`, checked against independent enumeration of
87	every outcome matrix in seven small cells. Exact gaps for two candidates at
88	\(p=\tfrac12\) are \(\tfrac14\), \(\tfrac{35}{256}\), about 0.0700 and about
89	0.0352 at 1, 4, 16 and 64 items; multiplied by \(\sqrt n\) these are 0.250,
90	0.273, 0.280 and 0.282. The value \(1/(2\sqrt\pi)\approx0.2821\) is the
91	standard Gaussian figure for the larger of two draws. The fixture verifies the
92	listed cells and no limit.
93	
94	Boundary: one generation, equal candidates, independent items. Accumulation
95	across generations is a simulation result, not an exact one.
96	
97	**Ceiling law.**
98	
99	> With labels flipped independently at rate \(\varepsilon<\tfrac12\), no
100	> predictor blind to the flips exceeds \(1-\varepsilon\) in expectation on
101	> observed labels. Let \(v\) be the controller's observed accuracy before any
102	> item of \(s\) is memorized. If it memorizes a share \(m/n\) of \(s\) chosen
103	> without regard to its outcomes, it scores \(m/n+(1-m/n)v\) on \(s\) and
104	> crosses the ceiling only when \(m/n>(1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)\). If it memorizes
105	> items it failed, which is what item-level feedback supplies, it scores
106	> \(v+m/n\) and crosses when \(m/n>1-\varepsilon-v\): the same threshold
107	> \((1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)\), now as a share of the failed items. Below the
108	> threshold a ceiling check is silent.
109	
110	Support: `ceiling_detection_threshold` and
111	`targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold`. With clean accuracy \(\tfrac45\) and
112	\(\varepsilon=\tfrac1{10}\): \(v=\tfrac{37}{50}\). Memorizing at random, the
113	check is silent below \(\tfrac8{13}\) of the set. Patching failures, it is
114	silent below \(\tfrac4{25}\) of the set, which is \(\tfrac8{13}\) of the failed
115	items. Both formulas assume a memorized item has no effect on any other item.
116	The nearest-neighbour learner in the second simulation did not satisfy that,
117	and it also did not reliably absorb a patch: at \(n=4000\) it patched a quarter
118	of the set and its reported score stayed at 0.759, below the 0.90 ceiling.
119	
120	**Observation on what item-level feedback selects.**
121	
122	> An item the controller fails is more likely than an average item to carry a
123	> wrong label, whenever the controller is better than chance:
124	> \(\Pr[\text{flipped}\mid\text{failed}]=\varepsilon a/(\varepsilon a+(1-\varepsilon)(1-a))\),
125	> which exceeds \(\varepsilon\) exactly when \(a>\tfrac12\). Feeding failures
126	> back concentrates label noise in what the next controller is built from.
127	
128	Support: `failed_item_noise_share`; \(\tfrac4{13}\) against a base rate of
129	\(\tfrac1{10}\) in the fixture. In the second simulation the measured share
130	among patched items was 20–29% against the same 10% base rate. This is the
131	reason the unchecked answer in the Proposer–Solver recipe (atlas §11) matters
132	once its output is fed back.
133	
134	Suggested closing sentence, matching the section's existing last line:
135	
136	> No unconditional claim is made that feedback lowers readout performance. In
137	> the simulations, score-only selection of fresh training batches raised it.
138	
139	## E. §7, after the definition of the order effect
140	
141	> For a controller \(\pi_g\) produced with feedback from \(s\), and a sealed set
142	> \(r\) from the same sampling law, define the readout gap
143	> \(\rho_g=V^{s}_{\pi_g}-V^{r}_{\pi_g}\). It compares two measurements of one
144	> controller, not two designs, so it is not a design difference. A gain series
145	> computed on \(s\) estimates the change in value plus the change in \(\rho\).
146	
147	## F. §11, the evaluation card
148	
149	Suggested amendment to item 6:
150	
151	> ... and whether any score feeds back into play *or into the production of a
152	> later controller*.
153	
154	Suggested additional item:
155	
156	> 10. **Feedback ledger:** for each evaluation set, its role (selection or
157	> readout), declared access class, score queries, items fed back, number and
158	> generation of readouts, and the rule that retires it.
159	
160	## G. `evaluation_game_testbed.md`, estimand table
161	
162	Suggested fifth row:
163	
164	| Estimand | Definition | It is not |
165	|---|---|---|
166	| Readout gap | \(\rho=V^{s}_\pi-V^{r}_\pi\), with \(s\) having fed judgment to the loop and \(r\) sealed | A baseline gain, or evidence that capability changed |
167	
168	Suggested section, placed after "Executable confirmation and adversarial
169	checks":
170	
171	> ### Feedback channel and multi-generation ledger
172	>
173	> `evaluation_game_feedback.py` extends the single split enforced by `confirm()`
174	> to a sequence of generations. Sets are declared with a role and an access
175	> class. Events record a score reaching the loop, items reaching the loop, or an
176	> experimenter reading a sealed set. Malformed declarations raise, including a
177	> readout set not declared sealed and identifiers shared across sets. Breaches
178	> of a well-formed declaration are recorded instead, and move the readout
179	> endpoint to `not_evaluated`: a breach is a finding about the run. Reads of the
180	> sealed set are budgeted, since a stop-or-continue decision taken on a readout
181	> is itself adaptive. Identifiers detect recorded overlap. They do not certify
182	> independence.
183	>
184	> ```powershell
185	> $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
186	> python scripts/verify_evaluation_game_feedback.py --output output/evaluation_game_feedback/feedback_v0_2.json
187	> python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_game_feedback.py -q
188	> ```
189	
190	## H. What is not delivered
191	
192	- `Feedback` is not implemented against `hive_lab` adapters or any external
193	  policy. The module checks declarations and arithmetic.
194	- No loop with a language model has been run. The first observed-controller
195	  study would pair a small model with a declared selection set and a sealed
196	  readout, and report the ledger.
197	- Partial leakage, where the loop learns failure categories and not items, has
198	  no fixture.
199	- The simulations fix one parameter set each. No sweep over candidate count,
200	  decay rate, or label-noise rate was run.

1	"""Exact, synthetic checks for evaluation-game estimands and acquisition design.
2	
3	Nothing in this module calls a model, grades a transcript, or infers intent.  It
4	uses finite rational fixtures to keep four quantities that are often called an
5	"evaluation result" separate: baseline gain, robust regret, measurement
6	discrimination, and strategic exploitability.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from fractions import Fraction as Q
12	from itertools import product
13	from typing import Iterable
14	
15	
16	def _tv(left: dict[str, Q], right: dict[str, Q]) -> Q:
17	    """Total variation distance of two finite distributions."""
18	
19	    return sum(abs(left.get(key, Q(0)) - right.get(key, Q(0)))
20	               for key in set(left) | set(right)) / 2
21	
22	
23	def _pushforward(distribution: dict[str, Q], kernel: dict[str, dict[str, Q]]) -> dict[str, Q]:
24	    """Apply a common finite Markov kernel to an already-produced record."""
25	
26	    if not distribution or sum(distribution.values()) != 1 or min(distribution.values()) < 0:
27	        raise ValueError("distribution must be nonnegative and sum to one")
28	    if not set(distribution) <= set(kernel):
29	        raise ValueError("kernel is missing a source record")
30	    if any(not row or sum(row.values()) != 1 or min(row.values()) < 0
31	           for row in kernel.values()):
32	        raise ValueError("every kernel row must be nonnegative and sum to one")
33	    output: dict[str, Q] = {}
34	    for source, mass in distribution.items():
35	        for target, probability in kernel[source].items():
36	            output[target] = output.get(target, Q(0)) + mass * probability
37	    return output

40	def _optimal_decision_value(
41	    states: tuple[str, ...], prior: dict[str, Q], actions: tuple[str, ...],
42	    observation_kernel: dict[str, dict[str, Q]],
43	) -> Q:
44	    """Exhaustively optimize a one-step decision rule respecting observations."""
45	
46	    observations = tuple(sorted({o for row in observation_kernel.values() for o in row}))
47	    best = Q(-1)
48	    for response in product(actions, repeat=len(observations)):
49	        policy = dict(zip(observations, response))
50	        value = sum(
51	            prior[state] * probability * int(policy[observation] == state)
52	            for state in states
53	            for observation, probability in observation_kernel[state].items()
54	        )
55	        best = max(best, value)
56	    return best

59	def baseline_gain_fixture() -> dict[str, Q]:
60	    """Compare two policies in the same revealed-state game and case law."""
61	
62	    states = ("left", "right")
63	    prior = {"left": Q(1, 2), "right": Q(1, 2)}
64	    revealed = {state: {state: Q(1)} for state in states}
65	    # Both receive the revealed state; only the candidate uses it.
66	    baseline = sum(prior[state] * int(state == "left") for state in states)
67	    candidate = _optimal_decision_value(states, prior, states, revealed)
68	    return {"baseline_value": baseline, "candidate_value": candidate,
69	            "baseline_gain": candidate - baseline}

124	def exploitability_fixture() -> dict[str, object]:
125	    """Exact strategic checks, including a deliberately restricted lower bound."""
126	
127	    actions = ("share", "take")
128	    payoff = {
129	        ("share", "share"): (Q(3), Q(3)), ("share", "take"): (Q(0), Q(5)),
130	        ("take", "share"): (Q(5), Q(0)), ("take", "take"): (Q(1), Q(1)),
131	    }
132	
133	    def gaps(profile: tuple[str, str], allowed: Iterable[str] = actions) -> tuple[Q, Q]:
134	        a, b = profile
135	        base = payoff[profile]
136	        return (
137	            max(payoff[(alternative, b)][0] for alternative in allowed) - base[0],
138	            max(payoff[(a, alternative)][1] for alternative in allowed) - base[1],
139	        )
140	
141	    equilibrium_set = tuple(profile for profile in product(actions, repeat=2)
142	                            if gaps(profile) == (Q(0), Q(0)))
143	    profile = ("share", "share")
144	    exact_gaps = gaps(profile)
145	    restricted_gaps = gaps(profile, ("share",))
146	    return {
147	        "adaptation_rule": "enumerate_pure_nash_then_lexicographically_select",
148	        "equilibrium_set": equilibrium_set,
149	        "selected_outcome": min(equilibrium_set),
150	        "profile_evaluated": profile,
151	        "exact_exploitability": max(exact_gaps),
152	        "restricted_best_response_lower_bound": max(restricted_gaps),
153	        "restricted_is_lower_bound": max(restricted_gaps) <= max(exact_gaps),

157	def zero_sum_primal_dual_fixture() -> dict[str, Q]:
158	    """Primal/dual certificate for a tiny zero-sum game, not a generic LP solver."""
159	
160	    # Matching pennies for the row player.  p=q=1/2 makes every pure response
161	    # worth zero, certifying maximin >= 0 and minimax <= 0 respectively.
162	    row_minimum = min(Q(1, 2) * Q(1) + Q(1, 2) * Q(-1),
163	                      Q(1, 2) * Q(-1) + Q(1, 2) * Q(1))
164	    column_maximum = max(Q(1, 2) * Q(1) + Q(1, 2) * Q(-1),
165	                         Q(1, 2) * Q(-1) + Q(1, 2) * Q(1))
166	    return {"primal_maximin_witness": row_minimum,
167	            "dual_minimax_witness": column_maximum,
168	            "certified_value": Q(0)}

171	def incentive_design_fixture() -> dict[str, object]:
172	    """Difficulty-matched, severity-stratified synthetic contrast and holdout.
173	
174	    The outcome law has *no latent intent variable*.  It is only a design check:
175	    within a difficulty/severity stratum, matched control minus incentive score
176	    estimates an incentive-response contrast while cancelling additive nuisance
177	    difficulty and grader-severity terms.
178	    """
179	
180	    difficulty_base = {"easy": Q(9, 10), "hard": Q(7, 10)}
181	    severity = {"lenient": Q(0), "strict": Q(-1, 10)}
182	    incentive_drop = {"easy": Q(1, 10), "hard": Q(3, 10)}
183	    rows = []
184	    for difficulty, grader in product(difficulty_base, severity):
185	        control = difficulty_base[difficulty] + severity[grader]
186	        incentive = control - incentive_drop[difficulty]
187	        rows.append({"split": "held_out", "difficulty": difficulty, "grader": grader,
188	                     "control_score": control, "incentive_score": incentive,
189	                     "paired_gap": control - incentive})
190	    by_difficulty = {
191	        difficulty: sum(r["paired_gap"] for r in rows if r["difficulty"] == difficulty)
192	        / sum(r["difficulty"] == difficulty for r in rows)
193	        for difficulty in difficulty_base
194	    }
195	    # Equal target weights over difficulty and grading severity.  Every matched
196	    # pair costs two scored responses; 12 pairs in each of four nuisance strata
197	    # costs 96 score operations.  This is a transparent balanced allocation,
198	    # not a claim that it is universally optimal under unknown variances.
199	    allocation = {f"{difficulty}:{grader}": 12
200	                  for difficulty, grader in product(difficulty_base, severity)}
201	    # With four equally weighted, equal-variance strata and fixed total cost,
202	    # the contrast variance is proportional to sum_h (1/4)^2 / n_h.  Enumerate
203	    # the feasible integer allocations rather than merely asserting balance.
204	    def objective(counts):
205	        return sum(Q(1, 16 * count) for count in counts)
206	    best_objective = min(
207	        objective((first, second, third, 48-first-second-third))
208	        for first in range(1, 46)
209	        for second in range(1, 47-first)
210	        for third in range(1, 48-first-second)
211	    )
212	    allocation_objective = objective(tuple(allocation.values()))
213	    return {
214	        "estimand": "held_out_incentive_response_contrast",
215	        "nuisance_structure": "score = difficulty + grader_severity + incentive + incentive_by_difficulty + noise",
216	        "matched_within": ("difficulty", "grader"),
217	        "scope": "four arithmetic cell values; enforced selection and confirmation are in evaluation_game_confirmation",
218	        "allocation_pairs": allocation,
219	        "planned_score_operations": 2 * sum(allocation.values()),
220	        "arithmetic_score_values": 2 * len(rows),
221	        "allocation_objective": allocation_objective,
222	        "allocation_objective_minimum": best_objective,
223	        "allocation_optimizes_equal_variance_contrast": allocation_objective == best_objective,
224	        "held_out_gaps_by_difficulty": by_difficulty,
225	        "held_out_incentive_by_difficulty_interaction": by_difficulty["hard"] - by_difficulty["easy"],
226	        "intent_identified": False,
227	        "falsifier": "A comparable interaction in negative-incentive controls, prompt inequivalence, or unblinded scoring invalidates the strategic interpretation.",
228	    }
229	
230	
231	def verify() -> dict[str, object]:
232	    """Run all exact fixtures and return machine-readable checks."""
233	
234	    gain = baseline_gain_fixture()
235	    regret = robust_regret_fixture()
236	    observed = observation_hide_fixture()
237	    player_hide = pre_action_hide_fixture()
238	    exploit = exploitability_fixture()
239	    duality = zero_sum_primal_dual_fixture()
240	    incentive = incentive_design_fixture()
241	    checks = {

244	        "observation_hide_is_common_and_contracts_discrimination": observed["same_kernel_for_all_policies"] and observed["data_processing_holds"] and observed["hidden_discrimination_gap"] == Q(0),
245	        "pre_action_hide_changes_decision_value": player_hide["game_change_value_loss"] == Q(1, 2),

247	        "equilibrium_outcome_is_reported_with_rule": exploit["selected_outcome"] == ("take", "take"),
248	        "primal_dual_witnesses_agree": duality["primal_maximin_witness"] == duality["dual_minimax_witness"] == duality["certified_value"],
249	        "heldout_incentive_interaction_is_explicit": incentive["held_out_incentive_by_difficulty_interaction"] == Q(1, 5),

251	        "incentive_fixture_does_not_identify_intent": not incentive["intent_identified"],
252	    }
253	    return {"evidence_status": "exact_synthetic_fixtures_not_model_or_agent_evidence",

1	"""Exact, synthetic checks for judgment-to-controller feedback.
2	
3	Nothing in this module calls a model, trains a learner, or runs an improvement
4	loop.  It types the channel by which a judgment reaches the process that
5	produces the next controller, and keeps the resulting *readout gap* separate
6	from baseline gain, robust regret, discrimination gap, and exploitability.
7	
8	Three access classes order that channel.  ``sealed`` returns nothing,
9	``score_only`` returns an aggregate count, ``item_level`` returns per-item
10	outcomes.  Each is a deterministic coarsening of the next, so the finite
11	data-processing inequality used for observation-only Hide applies to what the
12	loop can learn about its own failures.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from dataclasses import dataclass
18	from fractions import Fraction as Q
19	from itertools import product
20	from math import comb
21	
22	from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_testbed import _pushforward, _tv
23	
24	ACCESS_CLASSES = ("sealed", "score_only", "item_level")
25	ROLES = ("selection", "readout")
26	EVENT_KINDS = ("score_query", "item_feedback", "readout")
27	
28	
29	def access_kernel(access: str, items: int) -> dict[str, dict[str, Q]]:
30	    """Deterministic feedback kernel from per-item outcome records.
31	
32	    A record is a string of ``0``/``1`` of length ``items``.  The kernel says
33	    what reaches the loop, not what the evaluator stores.
34	    """
35	
36	    if access not in ACCESS_CLASSES:
37	        raise ValueError("unknown access class")
38	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
39	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
40	    kernel = {}
41	    for bits in product("01", repeat=items):
42	        record = "".join(bits)
43	        if access == "sealed":
44	            image = "sealed"
45	        elif access == "score_only":
46	            image = f"score={record.count('1')}"
47	        else:
48	            image = record
49	        kernel[record] = {image: Q(1)}
50	    return kernel
51	
52	
53	def access_order_fixture() -> dict[str, object]:
54	    """Two controllers with equal scores and different failures.
55	
56	    Item-level feedback separates them completely; score-only feedback cannot
57	    separate them at all.  A second pair with different scores is separated by
58	    both, and no pair is separated through a sealed set.
59	    """
60	
61	    same_score = ({"10": Q(1)}, {"01": Q(1)})
62	    different_score = ({"11": Q(1)}, {"00": Q(1)})
63	    gaps = {}
64	    for name, (left, right) in (("same_score", same_score),
65	                                ("different_score", different_score)):
66	        gaps[name] = {
67	            access: _tv(_pushforward(left, access_kernel(access, 2)),
68	                        _pushforward(right, access_kernel(access, 2)))
69	            for access in ACCESS_CLASSES
70	        }
71	    ordered = all(g["sealed"] <= g["score_only"] <= g["item_level"] for g in gaps.values())
72	    return {"operator_type": "judgment_to_controller_feedback_kernel",
73	            "gaps": gaps, "access_classes_ordered_by_coarsening": ordered,
74	            "acts_between_generations": True, "changes_recorded_evidence": False}
75	
76	
77	def _binomial_pmf(n: int, p: Q) -> list[Q]:
78	    return [Q(comb(n, j)) * p**j * (1 - p)**(n - j) for j in range(n + 1)]
79	
80	
81	def selection_inflation(items: int, candidates: int, p: Q) -> dict[str, Q]:
82	    """Exact one-generation over-report from keeping the best-scoring candidate.
83	
84	    Every candidate has the same true success probability ``p`` on each of
85	    ``items`` independent selection items, and candidates are independent.  The
86	    reported value is the selected candidate's score on those same items; the
87	    readout value is its expected score on untouched items, which is ``p``.
88	    This isolates the selection term.  It says nothing about real gains,
89	    persistence across generations, or correlated candidates.
90	    """
91	
92	    if type(items) is not int or type(candidates) is not int or items < 1 or candidates < 1:
93	        raise ValueError("items and candidates must be positive integers")
94	    if not 0 <= p <= 1:
95	        raise ValueError("p must be a probability")
96	    pmf = _binomial_pmf(items, p)
97	    cumulative, running = [], Q(0)
98	    for mass in pmf:
99	        running += mass
100	        cumulative.append(running)
101	    expected_max = sum(
102	        j * (cumulative[j]**candidates - (cumulative[j - 1]**candidates if j else Q(0)))
103	        for j in range(items + 1)
104	    )
105	    reported = expected_max / items
106	    return {"expected_reported": reported, "readout_value": p,
107	            "readout_gap": reported - p}
108	
109	
110	def observed_accuracy(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q) -> Q:
111	    """Accuracy against observed labels when labels flip independently."""
112	
113	    if not 0 <= clean_accuracy <= 1 or not 0 <= flip <= 1:
114	        raise ValueError("probabilities required")
115	    return clean_accuracy * (1 - flip) + (1 - clean_accuracy) * flip
116	
117	
118	def noise_ceiling(flip: Q) -> Q:
119	    """Best observed-label accuracy available to a predictor that cannot see
120	    which labels flipped."""
121	
122	    if not 0 <= flip <= 1:
123	        raise ValueError("flip must be a probability")
124	    return max(flip, 1 - flip)
125	
126	
127	def memorized_selection_score(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q, patch_share: Q) -> Q:
128	    """Selection-set score after memorizing a share of its observed labels.
129	
130	    The memorized items are chosen independently of whether the controller
131	    already got them right, so the remainder keep the base observed accuracy.
132	    Memorized items score one.  Collateral effects of a patch on other items
133	    are assumed absent, which a real learner need not satisfy.
134	    """
135	
136	    if not 0 <= patch_share <= 1:
137	        raise ValueError("patch share must lie in [0, 1]")
138	    base = observed_accuracy(clean_accuracy, flip)
139	    return patch_share + (1 - patch_share) * base
140	
141	
142	def targeted_patch_selection_score(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q, patch_share: Q) -> Q:
143	    """Selection-set score after memorizing failed items only.
144	
145	    This is what item-level feedback supplies: each patch turns one failed
146	    item into a pass and leaves every other item unchanged.  ``patch_share``
147	    is measured against the whole set and cannot exceed the failure share.
148	    """
149	
150	    base = observed_accuracy(clean_accuracy, flip)
151	    if not 0 <= patch_share <= 1 - base:
152	        raise ValueError("patch share must lie between zero and the failure share")
153	    return base + patch_share
154	
155	
156	def ceiling_detection_threshold(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q) -> Q:
157	    """Share of the set, memorized independently of outcomes, above which the
158	    selection score exceeds the noise ceiling.
159	
160	    Below this share the ceiling check is silent however much was memorized.
161	    """
162	
163	    base = observed_accuracy(clean_accuracy, flip)
164	    if base >= 1:
165	        raise ValueError("base observed accuracy must be below one")
166	    return max(Q(0), (noise_ceiling(flip) - base) / (1 - base))
167	
168	
169	def targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q) -> Q:
170	    """Share of the set, patched on failed items only, above which the
171	    selection score exceeds the noise ceiling.
172	
173	    As a share of the failed items this equals ``ceiling_detection_threshold``;
174	    as a share of the set it is smaller by the failure share.
175	    """
176	
177	    base = observed_accuracy(clean_accuracy, flip)
178	    if base >= 1:
179	        raise ValueError("base observed accuracy must be below one")
180	    return max(Q(0), noise_ceiling(flip) - base)
181	
182	
183	def failed_item_noise_share(clean_accuracy: Q, flip: Q) -> Q:
184	    """Probability that an item the base predictor fails has a flipped label.
185	
186	    The predictor errs on the clean label independently of the flip.  It fails
187	    the observed label either by being right about a flipped item or wrong
188	    about an unflipped one.
189	    """
190	
191	    wrong_because_flipped = flip * clean_accuracy
192	    wrong_unflipped = (1 - flip) * (1 - clean_accuracy)
193	    if wrong_because_flipped + wrong_unflipped == 0:
194	        raise ValueError("the predictor never fails an observed label")
195	    return wrong_because_flipped / (wrong_because_flipped + wrong_unflipped)
196	
197	
198	def noise_ceiling_fixture() -> dict[str, Q]:
199	    clean, flip = Q(4, 5), Q(1, 10)
200	    base = observed_accuracy(clean, flip)
201	    targeted = targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold(clean, flip)
202	    return {
203	        "clean_accuracy": clean, "flip_probability": flip,
204	        "base_observed_accuracy": base,
205	        "noise_ceiling": noise_ceiling(flip),
206	        "score_half_memorized": memorized_selection_score(clean, flip, Q(1, 2)),
207	        "score_fully_memorized": memorized_selection_score(clean, flip, Q(1)),
208	        "ceiling_detection_threshold": ceiling_detection_threshold(clean, flip),
209	        "targeted_threshold_share_of_set": targeted,
210	        "targeted_threshold_share_of_failures": targeted / (1 - base),
211	        "score_all_failures_patched": targeted_patch_selection_score(clean, flip, 1 - base),
212	        "failed_item_noise_share": failed_item_noise_share(clean, flip),
213	    }

232	def audit_ledger(sets, events, readout_budget, exhaustion_bound):
233	    """Check a multi-generation feedback ledger against its declarations.
234	
235	    Malformed declarations raise.  Breaches of a well-formed declaration are
236	    recorded, and move the affected endpoint to ``not_evaluated``, because a
237	    breach is a finding about the run and should survive into its report.
238	
239	    A ``score_query`` or ``item_feedback`` event means the result reached the
240	    loop.  A ``readout`` event means the experimenter read a sealed set; if a
241	    loop-affecting decision followed, that reading is itself adaptive, so the
242	    number of readouts is budgeted.  Identifiers detect recorded overlap only.
243	    They cannot certify that two differently named items are independent.
244	    """
245	
246	    if not sets:
247	        raise ValueError("at least one evaluation set must be declared")
248	    if type(readout_budget) is not int or readout_budget < 1:
249	        raise ValueError("readout budget must be a positive integer")
250	    if not exhaustion_bound > 0:
251	        raise ValueError("exhaustion bound must be positive")
252	    declared, owner = {}, {}
253	    for item in sets:
254	        if (not item.set_id or item.role not in ROLES or item.access not in ACCESS_CLASSES
255	                or not item.item_ids or len(set(item.item_ids)) != len(item.item_ids)):
256	            raise ValueError("invalid evaluation set declaration")
257	        if item.set_id in declared:
258	            raise ValueError("duplicate set identifier")
259	        if item.role == "readout" and item.access != "sealed":
260	            raise ValueError("a readout set must be declared sealed")
261	        for identifier in item.item_ids:
262	            if identifier in owner:
263	                raise ValueError("selection/readout identifiers overlap")
264	            owner[identifier] = item.set_id
265	        declared[item.set_id] = item
266	    if not any(item.role == "readout" for item in sets):
267	        raise ValueError("no readout set declared")
268	
269	    state = {
270	        set_id: {"role": item.role, "declared_access": item.access,
271	                 "size": len(item.item_ids), "score_queries": 0, "patches": 0,
272	                 "distinct_patched": set(), "readouts": [], "retired_at": None,
273	                 "breaches": []}
274	        for set_id, item in declared.items()
275	    }
276	    previous = None
277	    for event in events:

341	def divergence_flags(points, margin):
342	    """Compare selection-set and readout-set gains between permitted readouts.
343	
344	    ``points`` are ``(generation, selection_score, readout_score)`` at strictly
345	    increasing generations.  A flag voids claims resting on the selection set.
346	    It does not void the sealed readout.
347	    """
348	
349	    points = list(points)
350	    if len(points) < 2:
351	        raise ValueError("at least two readout points required")
352	    if not margin >= 0:
353	        raise ValueError("margin must be nonnegative")
354	    rows = []
355	    for (g0, s0, r0), (g1, s1, r1) in zip(points, points[1:]):
356	        if type(g0) is not int or type(g1) is not int or g1 <= g0:
357	            raise ValueError("generations must be strictly increasing integers")
358	        if not all(0 <= value <= 1 for value in (s0, r0, s1, r1)):
359	            raise ValueError("scores must lie in [0, 1]")
360	        divergence = (s1 - s0) - (r1 - r0)
361	        rows.append({"from_generation": g0, "to_generation": g1,
362	                     "selection_gain": s1 - s0, "readout_gain": r1 - r0,
363	                     "divergence": divergence, "readout_gap_at_end": s1 - r1,
364	                     "flagged": divergence > margin})
365	    return rows

import json
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from itertools import accumulate, product
from math import comb

import pytest

from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_feedback import EvalSet, LoopEvent, audit_ledger
from spiral_ln.evaluation_feedback_composition import (
    CANDIDATES, FIELDS, LOCATIONS, Acquisition, Declaration, Game, Item, Judgment,
    Op, Policy, Record, Utility, Acquired, apply, apply_sequence, cap, commutation_alphabet,
    compile_ledger, controller, describe_policy, enumerate_states, feedback,
    first_witness, footprint_audit, footprints_disjoint, grant, hide, item_outcomes,
    judge, ledger_verdict, lookup_policy, make_record, observe, payoff, play, project,
    readout, readout_gap, readout_gap_rescore_fixture, repeat, repeat_carry_fixture,
    rescore, restrict, set_value, typecheck, typing_ledger_equivalence, verify,
)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def report():
    return verify()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def states():
    return enumerate_states()


# --- the executable record ---------------------------------------------------

def test_play_uses_observation_overrides_and_legal_fallback():
    s1 = Item("s1", "S", "right")
    assert play(Game(LOCATIONS, True), lookup_policy("follow"), s1).action == "right"
    assert play(Game(LOCATIONS, False), lookup_policy("follow"), s1).observation == "hidden"
    assert play(Game(LOCATIONS, False), lookup_policy("follow"), s1).action == "left"
    assert play(Game(("left",), True), lookup_policy("follow"), s1).action == "left"
    memorized = lookup_policy("always_left", (("s1", "right"),))
    assert play(Game(LOCATIONS, False), memorized, s1).action == "right"


def test_judgment_handles_redaction_flips_and_cost():
    assert judge(Judgment(), Acquired("s0", "S", "left", "left")) == 1
    assert judge(Judgment(), Acquired("s0", "S", "right", "left")) == 0
    assert judge(Judgment(), Acquired("s0", "S", None, "left")) is None
    assert judge(Judgment(("s0",)), Acquired("s0", "S", "left", "left")) == 0
    assert judge(Judgment((), Q(1)), Acquired("s1", "S", "right", "right")) == 0
    assert judge(Judgment((), Q(1)), Acquired("s0", "S", "right", "left")) == -1


def test_set_values_and_readout_gap():
    assert (set_value(make_record("always_left"), "S"), readout_gap(make_record("always_left"))) == (Q(1, 2), 0)
    assert set_value(make_record("follow"), "S") == set_value(make_record("follow"), "R") == 1
    assert set_value(make_record("follow", revealed=False), "S") == Q(1, 2)
    assert set_value(make_record(redacted=("S",)), "S") is None
    assert readout_gap(make_record(redacted=("S",))) is None
    assert item_outcomes(make_record(), "S") == (("s0", "left", Q(1)), ("s1", "left", Q(0)))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unknown set"):
        item_outcomes(make_record(), "X")


def test_item_level_feedback_patches_failed_items_only():
    patched = apply(feedback("S", "item_level"), make_record("always_left"))
    assert patched.pi.overrides == (("s1", "right"),) and patched.generation == 1
    untouched = apply(feedback("S", "item_level"), make_record("always_left", flipped=("s1",)))
    assert untouched.pi == lookup_policy("always_left")
    costed = apply(feedback("S", "item_level"), make_record("always_right", judgment_cost=Q(1)))
    assert costed.pi.overrides == (("s0", "left"), ("s1", "left"))


def test_score_only_feedback_takes_strict_improvements_and_keeps_incumbent_on_ties():
    improved = apply(feedback("S", "score_only", CANDIDATES), make_record("always_left"))
    assert improved.pi == lookup_policy("follow") and improved.generation == 1
    tied = apply(feedback("S", "score_only", CANDIDATES), make_record("always_left", revealed=False))
    assert tied.pi == lookup_policy("always_left")
    assert apply(feedback("S", "score_only"), make_record("always_left")).pi == lookup_policy("always_left")


def test_sealed_feedback_only_advances_generation():
    for set_id in ("S", "R"):
        after = apply(feedback(set_id, "sealed"), make_record("always_left"))
        assert after.pi == lookup_policy("always_left") and after.generation == 1


def test_feedback_learns_nothing_from_a_redacted_set():
    redacted = make_record("always_left", redacted=("S",))
    for access in ("item_level", "score_only"):
        after = apply(feedback("S", access, CANDIDATES), redacted)
        assert after.pi == redacted.pi and after.generation == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize("op, record, message", [
    (feedback("X", "item_level"), make_record(), "undeclared"),
    (feedback("R", "item_level"), make_record(), "readout set"),
    (feedback("R", "score_only", CANDIDATES), make_record(), "readout set"),
    (feedback("S", "item_level"), make_record(selection_access="score_only"), "exceeds the declared access"),

def _max_distribution(items, count, p):
    if count == 0:
        return {0: Q(1)}
    pmf = [Q(comb(items, j)) * p**j * (1 - p)**(items - j) for j in range(items + 1)]
    cdf = list(accumulate(pmf))
    return {j: cdf[j]**count - (cdf[j - 1]**count if j else Q(0)) for j in range(items + 1)}

    expected_first = sum(Q(j, items) * m for j, m in first.items())
    expected_second = sum(Q(j, items) * m for j, m in doubled.items())
    exceeds = sum(first[a] * sum(m for b, m in fresh.items() if b > a) for a in first)

    assert fixture["reset"]["prob_second_exceeds_first"] == fixture["reset"]["prob_first_exceeds_second"]
    assert fixture["carry"]["exchangeable"] == (candidates == 1)
    lower_bound = (1 - p)**(items * candidates) * (1 - (1 - p)**(items * (candidates - 1)))
    assert fixture["carry"]["prob_second_exceeds_first"] >= lower_bound
    assert (fixture["generation_mean_difference"] > 0) == (candidates > 1)
