# Composition laws for Feedback

Version 0.1 — 2026-10-12. Companion to
[evaluation_design_calculus.md](evaluation_design_calculus.md) (§3 footprints,
§4 Repeat, §5 disjoint-update law, §7 order effects) and
[evaluation_feedback_insertions.md](evaluation_feedback_insertions.md)
(\(\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,q}\), the ledger). Nothing here calls a model or
observes a controller. Every statement is either an algebraic identity with a
proof or an exhaustive check on an enumerated finite model; the evidence line
under each proposition says which.

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
python scripts/verify_evaluation_feedback_composition.py --output output/evaluation_feedback_composition/composition_v0_1.json
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_feedback_composition.py -q
```

Receipt: `output/evaluation_feedback_composition/composition_v0_1.json`
(22 checks, `all_passed: true`, source hashes). Tests: 99.

## 1. The executable record

`src/spiral_ln/evaluation_feedback_composition.py` implements \(\mathcal E\)
as a frozen record with twelve fields: `game.legal`, `game.revealed`,
`game.utility`, `game.budget`, `game.horizon`, `game.carry` (\(G\), the
two-location game played once per item); `pi` (\(\Pi\): a lookup table from
observation to action plus per-item overrides, so patching an item is
memorizing its identifier); `items` (\(D\): `s0,s1` in the selection set `S`
and `r0,r1` in the readout set `R`); `acquisition` (\(Z\): the privileged
record, with the action redacted on named sets); `judgment` (\(J\): one for
the resource, inverted on flipped items, less a cost for choosing right;
undefined on a redacted record); `generation` (\(g\)); `declarations` (role
and access class per set). \(\mathcal A\) appears only in Proposition 4; \(C\)
is not modeled.

Each operator is a pure function with a declared footprint. Restrict, Grant,
Cap, Hide (player-facing), Observe (observation-only), Controller, Rescore,
Payoff (with or without also installing the utility as the judgment) and
Repeat write the fields their names suggest and read at most what they write.
\(\operatorname{Feedback}_{S,q}\) reads `game.legal`, `game.revealed`, `pi`,
`items`, `acquisition`, `judgment`, `declarations`, `generation` and writes
`pi`, `generation`: item-level access returns the per-item vector and
overrides every item judged nonpositive with the other action; score-only
access returns the sum for the incumbent and three fixed candidates and keeps
the first maximizer; sealed access returns nothing and only advances \(g\).
Applying Feedback to a set whose declaration does not permit it raises: that
application is ill-typed, not a breach.

## 2. The disjoint-update law and its witnesses

**Proposition 1 (disjoint-update law).** Call a footprint *sound* if the
operator changes no field outside \(W\) and the new values of \(W\) are a
function of the old values of \(R\). If \(a,b\) have sound footprints with
\(W_a\cap(R_b\cup W_b)=\emptyset\) and \(W_b\cap(R_a\cup W_a)=\emptyset\), then
\(a;b=b;a\) on every record (\(a;b\) applies \(a\) first).

*Proof.* Fix \(x\). Fields outside \(W_a\cup W_b\) are untouched in both
orders. For \(f\in W_a\): in \(a;b\), \(a\) writes \(f\) from \(x|_{R_a}\) and
\(b\) leaves it (\(f\notin W_b\)); in \(b;a\), \(b\) leaves \(R_a\) unchanged
(\(W_b\cap R_a=\emptyset\)), so \(a\) writes the same value. Symmetrically for
\(W_b\). \(\square\)

Boundary: sufficient only, and about the record; it does not say two
mechanisms' effects on behaviour are additive (calculus §5). Fixture:
`footprint_audit` verifies soundness of all 13 footprints on the 384
enumerated records (write side on every record; read side by grouping records
with equal \(R\)-projection and requiring equal \(W\)-images), and
`commutation_audit` checks every disjoint pair on every record. Evidence:
algebraic identity (the proposition); finite verified example (that the
model's footprints are sound and the law's instances hold on it).

**Proposition 2 (commutation table).** On the 384 records, of the 78
off-diagonal unordered pairs of the 13 operators, 60 have disjoint footprints
and commute, 15 do not commute, and 3 commute despite overlapping footprints.
The non-commuting pairs, with the field in which the two orders differ:

| Pair | Differ in | First witness (receipt) |
|---|---|---|
| Grant\(_2\), Cap\(_5\) | `game.budget` | budget 4: grant-then-cap 5, cap-then-grant 6 (calculus §5) |
| Rescore\(_j\), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | always-left, flip `s1`: rescore-then-feedback learns nothing; feedback-then-rescore memorizes `s1` |
| Observe (redact `S`), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | observe-then-feedback learns nothing; feedback-then-observe memorizes `s1` |
| Controller\(_\pi\), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | both write \(\Pi\); the second write determines it |
| Hide (player), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | follow: hide-then-feedback memorizes `s1`; the other order does not |
| Restrict\(_{\{\text{left}\}}\), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | same shape as Hide: the forced action fails and is patched |
| Payoff with training, Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | the installed judgment changes what is selected or patched |
| Rescore\(_j\), Payoff with training | `judgment` | both write \(J\); the second write wins |
| Feedback (item), Feedback (score) | `pi` only | the two update rules do not commute |

Payoff without training commutes with Feedback (it writes only
`game.utility`), as do Grant, Cap and Repeat: Repeat commuting at design time
says nothing about the aggregation unit, which is Proposition 4. Commuting
despite overlap: sealed Feedback with item-level and with score-only Feedback
(both write `generation`; \(g+1+1\) is order-free) and the two Payoffs (same
utility). In Rescore-then-Feedback versus Feedback-then-Rescore the final
\(J\) is the same and only \(\Pi\) differs: rescoring before feedback changes
what the loop learns, after it changes only the readout (\(V^S\) is 1 versus
1/2 in the hand-computed test). Evidence: finite verified example; nothing is
claimed outside the enumerated records and the two fixed update rules.

## 3. Typing as ledger audit

`compile_ledger` maps a design expression with declarations to the
`(sets, events)` input of `audit_ledger`: item-level Feedback records one
`item_feedback` naming every item of the set (the vector reached the loop,
whatever the rule did with it); score-only Feedback records one `score_query`
per policy scored; sealed Feedback records nothing; Readout\(_t\) records one
`readout`; every other operator is outside the channel. The context
\(\Gamma\) carries declarations, cumulative patches, retirement and readouts:

- (F-SEL) \(\Gamma\vdash\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,q}\), \(q>\)sealed, iff \(s\)
  is declared with role selection, access\((s)\ge q\), and \(s\) is not
  retired; item-level adds \(|s|\) to patches\((s)\), and \(s\) retires once
  patches\(/|s|\) exceeds the bound (the crossing step is itself typed).
- (F-SEALED) \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,\text{sealed}}\) is typed; \(\Gamma'=\Gamma\).
- (RO) \(\operatorname{Readout}_t\) iff role\((t)=\)readout (hence sealed) and
  the count stays within the readout budget.
- (NEUTRAL) every other operator is typed with \(\Gamma'=\Gamma\).

**Proposition 3.** Over all 22,143 sequences of length \(\le4\) from the
nine-symbol alphabet {Feedback\(_{S,q}\), Feedback\(_{R,q}\) for the three
access classes, Readout\(_R\), Readout\(_S\), Rescore} under three declaration
contexts (`S` declared item-level, score-only or sealed; `R` sealed; budget 2;
bound 1 with \(|S|=2\)), a sequence is well-typed iff `audit_ledger` returns
`declarations_respected = True` (2,581 respected, 11,462 breached, 8,100
raise). Evidence: finite verified example.

Two findings. (i) The ledger has two rejection modes. Every sequence
containing Readout\(_S\) makes `audit_ledger` raise ("readout events apply to
readout sets only") instead of recording a breach, so such a run has no report
at all, unlike the other breaches, which its docstring says should survive
into the report; the equivalence counts a raise as not respected. (ii) The
literal rule "Feedback\(_{s,q}\) requires role selection and access \(\ge q\)"
is too strict at \(q=\)sealed: the ledger has no event for a sealed read, so
Feedback\(_{R,\text{sealed}}\), through which nothing crosses, is invisible to
it. With the literal role premise the equivalence fails on exactly 1,414
sequences, all respected runs containing Feedback\(_{R,\text{sealed}}\) and
nothing else ill-typed. (F-SEALED) drops the premise; `audit_ledger` is not
patched.

## 4. Repeat with a carry map

**Proposition 4 (generations joined by Feedback are not blocks).** Let
\(K\ge2\) candidates each succeed independently with probability
\(p\in(0,1)\) on each of \(n\) items of \(s\); generation 1 keeps the best by
score (\(S_1\)); the carry map of \(\operatorname{Repeat}_{2,m}\) carries
\(\Pi_2\) into generation 2's pool with \(K-1\) fresh candidates (\(S_2\)).
Then \(S_2\) is the maximum of \(2K-1\) i.i.d. scores, so
\(\mathbb E S_2=p+\gamma(n,2K-1,p)>p+\gamma(n,K,p)=\mathbb E S_1\) with
\(\gamma\) the gap of `selection_inflation`; \(S_2\ge S_1\) pointwise with
\(\Pr[S_2>S_1]\ge(1-p)^{nK}\bigl(1-(1-p)^{n(K-1)}\bigr)>0\); hence
\((S_1,S_2)\) is not exchangeable, and the mean over generations exceeds what
the same \(\mathcal A\) reports over independent blocks by
\((\gamma(n,2K-1,p)-\gamma(n,K,p))/2>0\), while the sealed readout stays at
\(p\): the whole expected gain \(\mathbb E[S_2-S_1]\) is a change in \(\rho\).
Under the reset map \(S_1,S_2\) are i.i.d. and the two aggregations agree.

*Proof.* The kept candidate's realized outcomes on \(s\) are fixed, so its
generation-2 score is \(S_1\); the pool maximum is the maximum of the original
\(K\) and the fresh \(K-1\) i.i.d. scores. Monotonicity of the maximum gives
\(S_2\ge S_1\); "all \(nK\) generation-1 outcomes fail and some fresh outcome
succeeds" has the stated probability and forces \(S_2>S_1\); unequal means
rule out exchangeability. \(\square\)

Fixture: `repeat_carry_fixture` enumerates every outcome matrix. At
\(n=1,K=2,p=1/2\): \(\mathbb ES_1=3/4\), \(\mathbb ES_2=7/8\), generation mean
\(13/16\) under carry against \(3/4\) over independent blocks,
\(\Pr[S_2>S_1]=1/8\), \(\Pr[S_1>S_2]=0\), \(\rho\) equal to \(1/4\) then
\(3/8\). Three further cells agree with `selection_inflation` at \(2K-1\).
Evidence: algebraic identity under the stated model; finite verified example
for the numbers. Boundary: two generations, equal candidates, independent
items, a carry map that re-scores the incumbent on the same items; the full
multi-generation chain is built elsewhere.

## 5. Readout gap under Rescore

**Proposition 5.** \(\rho=V^s-V^r\) is a function of \((G,\Pi,D,Z,J)\);
\(\operatorname{Rescore}_j\) writes \(J\) only and \(\operatorname{Feedback}\)
writes \(\Pi\) and \(g\). So \(\rho\) can change with \(\Pi\) and \(g\) fixed
and no event in the ledger, and a change in \(\rho\) alone does not identify
feedback. Fixture (`readout_gap_rescore_fixture`, always-left controller,
\(\rho=0\)): rescoring `r1` moves \(\rho\) to \(-1/2\); rescoring `s1` moves it
to \(+1/2\), exactly the \(\rho\) that \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{S,\text{item}}\)
produces by memorizing `s1`. The ledger separates the two (0 against 2 patches
on `S`); \(\rho\) does not. Evidence: algebraic identity (the footprint
argument); finite verified example (the values).

## 6. What is general and what is enumerated

Proven in general: Propositions 1, 4 and 5 as stated. Checked only on
enumerated cases: that the model's footprints are sound (384 records), the
commutation table (13 operators, 384 records), the typing/ledger equivalence
(22,143 sequences, three contexts), and every number above. The commutation
witnesses concern one fixed pair of update rules on one tiny game; another
patch or selection rule may commute, or fail to, with different operators, and
the audit must be rerun for it. All laws concern design-time transformations
of the record, not what a learned controller does with what the channel
transmits. No model was run.

observation to action plus per-item overrides, so patching an item memorizes its identifier); `items`
(\(D\): `s0,s1` in the selection set `S`, `r0,r1` in the readout set `R`); `acquisition` (\(Z\): the
privileged record, with the action redacted on named sets); `judgment` (\(J\): one for the resource,
inverted on flipped items, less a cost for choosing right; undefined on a redacted record);
`generation` (\(g\)); `declarations` (role and access class per set). \(\mathcal A\) appears only in
Proposition 4; \(C\) is not modeled.

Each operator is a pure function with a declared footprint. Restrict, Grant, Cap, Hide
(player-facing), Observe (observation-only), Controller, Rescore, Payoff (with or without also
installing the utility as the judgment) and Repeat write the fields their names suggest and read at
most what they write. \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{S,q}\) reads `game.legal`, `game.revealed`, `pi`,
`items`, `acquisition`, `judgment`, `declarations`, `generation` and writes `pi`, `generation`:
item-level access returns the per-item vector and overrides every item judged nonpositive with the
other action; score-only access returns the sum for the incumbent and three fixed candidates and keeps
the first maximizer; sealed access returns nothing and only advances \(g\). Applying Feedback to a set
whose declaration does not permit it raises: that application is ill-typed, not a breach.

outside \(W\) and the new values of \(W\) are a function of the old values of \(R\). If \(a,b\) have
sound footprints with \(W_a\cap(R_b\cup W_b)=\emptyset\) and \(W_b\cap(R_a\cup W_a)=\emptyset\), then

leaves \(R_a\) unchanged (\(W_b\cap R_a=\emptyset\)), so \(a\) writes the same value. Symmetrically

| Controller\(_\pi\), Feedback (item, score) | `pi` only | both write \(\Pi\); the second write determines it |

the hand-computed test). Evidence: finite verified example; nothing is claimed outside the enumerated
records and the two fixed update rules.

`compile_ledger` maps a design expression with declarations to the `(sets, events)` input of
`audit_ledger`: item-level Feedback records one `item_feedback` naming every item of the set (the vector
reached the loop, whatever the rule did with it); score-only Feedback records one `score_query` per
policy scored; sealed Feedback records nothing; Readout\(_t\) records one `readout`; every other
operator is outside the channel. \(\Gamma\) carries declarations, cumulative patches, retirement and
readouts per set:

  selection, access\((s)\ge q\), and \(s\) is not retired; item-level adds \(|s|\) to patches\((s)\),
  and \(s\) retires once patches\(/|s|\) exceeds the bound (the crossing step is itself typed).

crosses, is invisible to it. With the literal role premise the equivalence fails on exactly 1,414

(F-SEALED) drops the premise; `audit_ledger` is not patched.

loop learns; after, only the readout: the final \(J\) agrees, \(\Pi\) differs, and \(V^S\) is 1 against
1/2 in the hand-computed test. Evidence: finite verified example, for these records and update rules only.

## 3. Typing as ledger audit

`compile_ledger` maps a design expression with declarations to the `(sets, events)` input of
`audit_ledger`: item-level Feedback records one `item_feedback` naming every item of the set (the vector
reached the loop, whatever the rule did with it); score-only records one `score_query` per policy
scored; sealed records nothing; Readout\(_t\) records one `readout`; other operators are outside the
channel. \(\Gamma\) carries declarations, cumulative patches, retirement and readouts per set:

- (F-SEL) \(\Gamma\vdash\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,q}\), \(q>\)sealed, iff \(s\) is declared selection,
  access\((s)\ge q\), and \(s\) not retired; item-level adds \(|s|\) to patches\((s)\), and \(s\) retires
  once patches\(/|s|\) exceeds the bound (the crossing step is itself typed).
- (F-SEALED) \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,\text{sealed}}\) is typed, \(\Gamma'=\Gamma\); likewise (NEUTRAL) every other operator.
- (RO) \(\operatorname{Readout}_t\) iff role\((t)=\)readout (hence sealed) and the count stays within the readout budget.

**Proposition 3.** Over all 22,143 sequences of length \(\le4\) from the nine-symbol alphabet
{Feedback\(_{S,q}\), Feedback\(_{R,q}\) for the three access classes, Readout\(_R\), Readout\(_S\),
Rescore} under three declaration contexts (`S` declared item-level, score-only or sealed; `R` sealed;
budget 2; bound 1 with \(|S|=2\)), a sequence is well-typed iff `audit_ledger` returns
`declarations_respected = True` (2,581 respected, 11,462 breached, 8,100 raise). Evidence: finite verified example.

Two findings. (i) The ledger has two rejection modes: every sequence containing Readout\(_S\) makes
`audit_ledger` raise ("readout events apply to readout sets only") rather than record a breach, so that
run gets no report, unlike the other breaches, which its docstring says should survive into the report;
the equivalence counts a raise as not respected. (ii) The literal rule "Feedback\(_{s,q}\) requires role
selection and access \(\ge q\)" is too strict at \(q=\)sealed: a sealed read has no event, so
Feedback\(_{R,\text{sealed}}\) is invisible to the ledger; with the literal premise the equivalence fails
on exactly 1,414 sequences, all respected runs containing it and nothing else ill-typed. (F-SEALED)
drops the premise; `audit_ledger` is not patched.

## 4. Repeat with a carry map

**Proposition 4 (generations joined by Feedback are not blocks).** Let \(K\ge2\) candidates each
succeed independently with probability \(p\in(0,1)\) on each of \(n\) items of \(s\); generation 1
keeps the best by score (\(S_1\)); the carry map of \(\operatorname{Repeat}_{2,m}\) carries \(\Pi_2\)
into generation 2's pool with \(K-1\) fresh candidates (\(S_2\)). Then \(S_2\) is the maximum of
\(2K-1\) i.i.d. scores, so \(\mathbb E S_2=p+\gamma(n,2K-1,p)>p+\gamma(n,K,p)=\mathbb E S_1\) with
\(\gamma\) the gap of `selection_inflation`; \(S_2\ge S_1\) pointwise with
\(\Pr[S_2>S_1]\ge(1-p)^{nK}\bigl(1-(1-p)^{n(K-1)}\bigr)>0\); hence \((S_1,S_2)\) is not exchangeable,
and the mean over generations exceeds what the same \(\mathcal A\) reports over independent blocks by
\((\gamma(n,2K-1,p)-\gamma(n,K,p))/2>0\), while the sealed readout stays at \(p\): the whole expected
gain \(\mathbb E[S_2-S_1]\) is a change in \(\rho\). Under the reset map \(S_1,S_2\) are i.i.d. and
the two aggregations agree.

*Proof.* The kept candidate's realized outcomes on \(s\) are fixed, so its generation-2 score is
\(S_1\), and the pool maximum is the maximum of the original \(K\) and the fresh \(K-1\) i.i.d. scores.
Monotonicity gives \(S_2\ge S_1\); "all \(nK\) generation-1 outcomes fail and some fresh outcome
succeeds" has the stated probability and forces \(S_2>S_1\); unequal means rule out exchangeability. \(\square\)

Fixture: `repeat_carry_fixture` enumerates every outcome matrix. At \(n=1,K=2,p=1/2\):
\(\mathbb ES_1=3/4\), \(\mathbb ES_2=7/8\), generation mean \(13/16\) under carry against \(3/4\) over
independent blocks, \(\Pr[S_2>S_1]=1/8\), \(\Pr[S_1>S_2]=0\), \(\rho=1/4\) then \(3/8\); three further
cells agree with `selection_inflation` at \(2K-1\). Evidence: algebraic identity under the stated
model; finite verified example for the numbers. Boundary: two generations, equal candidates, independent
items, a carry map re-scoring the incumbent on the same items; the multi-generation chain is built elsewhere.

## 5. Readout gap under Rescore

**Proposition 5.** \(\rho=V^s-V^r\) is a function of \((G,\Pi,D,Z,J)\); \(\operatorname{Rescore}_j\)
writes \(J\) only, \(\operatorname{Feedback}\) writes \(\Pi\) and \(g\). So \(\rho\) can change with
\(\Pi\), \(g\) fixed and no ledger event, and a change in \(\rho\) alone does not identify feedback.
Fixture (`readout_gap_rescore_fixture`, always-left controller, \(\rho=0\)): rescoring `r1` moves
\(\rho\) to \(-1/2\); rescoring `s1` moves it to \(+1/2\), exactly the \(\rho\) that
\(\operatorname{Feedback}_{S,\text{item}}\) produces by memorizing `s1`. The ledger separates the two
(0 against 2 patches on `S`); \(\rho\) does not. Evidence: algebraic identity (footprints); finite verified example (values).

## 6. What is general and what is enumerated

Proven in general: Propositions 1, 4 and 5 as stated. Checked only on enumerated cases: footprint
soundness (384 records), the commutation table (13 operators, 384 records), the typing/ledger
equivalence (22,143 sequences, three contexts), and every number above. The witnesses concern one pair
of update rules on one tiny game; another patch or selection rule needs the audit rerun. All laws are
design-time transformations of the record, not what a learned controller does with what the channel
transmits. No model was run.

- Grant₂/Cap₅ (budget 4 → 5 vs 6)

**General vs finite.** Proven in general: Prop 1 (disjoint-update law given sound footprints), Prop 4, Prop 5. Finite only: footprint soundness, the commutation table and witnesses, typing/ledger equivalence, all numbers. Paper repeats the design-time boundary; no model evidence claimed.
